objective: Assess commit 1c253b4, which makes @jdxcode/mise a trusted dev dependency and runs mise through bunx in the git hooks.
scope: Diff: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/1d4ee015-2de1-5dc0-aa17-15643c104828/scratchpad/mise-dep.diff (repository /home/user/holyagent-docs, branch claude/intelligent-dijkstra-x7njap). Files: package.json (devDependency @jdxcode/mise ^2026.10.24 and trustedDependencies), bun.lock, lefthook.yml (pre-commit jobs now run `bunx mise run ...`), docs/development.md.

Questions to settle with evidence: (1) trustedDependencies lets @jdxcode/mise's preinstall (node installArchSpecificPackage.js) run on every bun install; its platform package is fetched at install time and is not pinned by bun.lock — what is the supply-chain exposure and is the version range (^) appropriate versus an exact pin as the repo pins its other devDependencies? (2) `bunx mise` in lefthook: when node_modules/.bin/mise is missing (fresh clone before bun install, or install failure), does bunx resolve and execute the unrelated npm package named `mise` instead of @jdxcode/mise? If so that is a code-execution path from the registry in a git hook; propose the safe form (for example `bun x --no-install`, `bunx --package @jdxcode/mise mise`, or calling node_modules/.bin/mise through a Bun script). Check Bun's documentation for bunx resolution and flags; look facts up rather than assume. (3) Windows behavior of the hook form.
constraints: Read-only. Report each finding blocking or non-blocking with a concrete exploit or failure path and the minimal fix; stop and report when done.

criteria.text: The bunx resolution and the trusted install script are each judged safe or not with evidence

result:
result: Not safe to merge yet. One blocking regression: the new explicit `trustedDependencies` list silently turns off the install scripts of `lefthook` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. The `bunx mise` fallback and the trusted `@jdxcode/mise` script are both non-blocking, with hardening recommended. I ran nothing, because this session has no Bash tool. The conclusions come from reading the diff, repo files, Bun docs and source, and the npm registry.

built-in `/security-review`: it could not run. Its `git diff origin/HEAD...` failed with "unknown revision" because `origin/HEAD` does not exist here. Everything below is a manual source-to-sink review of commit 1c253b4 only, from the diff file.

changed: none (read-only).

checks: none run (no shell). Facts below were fetched from the sources named in the evidence lines.

blockers:
1. `trustedDependencies` now disables `lefthook` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` install scripts (confirmed from docs, not run). This is a regression, not an exploit.
   - Bun's docs say that defining `trustedDependencies` in `package.json` replaces the built-in default list rather than extending it. The commit sets the list to `["@jdxcode/mise"]` only.
   - Bun's default list contains both `lefthook` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. The lockfile marks both `"hasInstallScript": true` (`bun.lock` lines 47 and 235 in the main checkout, before this commit). Both relied on the default list until now.
   - CI runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and then `bun run claude plugin validate`. That needs the claude-code postinstall to have linked the native binary, and `ci.yml` calls the binary "integrity-checked". After this commit, CI most likely fails with an exec error, and local `bun run claude` fails the same way.
   - `lefthook` loses its postinstall too. Hook installation still goes through `bunx lefthook install` in the `prepare` script, so the impact there is smaller.
   - Minimal fix: `"trustedDependencies": ["@anthropic-ai/claude-code", "lefthook", "@jdxcode/mise"]`. Then verify with a clean `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun run claude --version`.

notes:
- (Q2) `bunx mise` resolution: acceptable fail-closed behavior, with one hardening change recommended (non-blocking, low).
  - Bun puts the `node_modules/.bin` directories ahead of the system PATH and looks the bin name `mise` up there. Because the name is unscoped, the system PATH is searched too. The locally installed `@jdxcode/mise` therefore wins when present, and a global mise is used if there is no local one.
  - Only if neither exists does `bunx` install the npm package named `mise` into its global cache and run it.
  - That package is not unrelated. It is jdx's own, at the same version 2026.10.24, published by GitHub Actions with provenance. The mise docs say to install `mise`, "not the older `@jdxcode/mise` package".
  - `bunx` does not run lifecycle scripts for cache installs, and `trustedDependencies` has no effect there (Bun issues #5552 and #8154). The package's `bin/mise` is removed at pack time and only created by the preinstall. So the fallback should fail with a missing-binary error rather than run anything. This is inferred from those issues and was not run here.
  - The residual risk is that the fallback is an unpinned, lockfile-less run of registry code inside a git hook. If a future `mise` publish ships a real `bin/mise` in its tarball, it would execute without scripts being needed. That needs registry or maintainer compromise.
  - Safe form: `bunx --no-install mise run ...`, with the flag before the package name. Bun's source shows that when no binary is found it exits with "Could not find an existing 'mise' binary to run. Stopping because --no-install was passed."
  - `bunx --package @jdxcode/mise mise` is not safer. It keeps the same local-then-registry order and would fetch `@jdxcode/mise@latest` unpinned.
- (Q1) The trusted `@jdxcode/mise` preinstall: acceptable for a dev dependency, with caveats (non-blocking).
  - What runs: `node installArchSpecificPackage.js`, about 1.8 KB. Judging by mise's `scripts/release-npm.sh` (the shipped 2026.10.24 script itself was not readable), it spawns `npm install --no-save @jdxcode/mise-<os>-<arch>@<same version>` with `shell: true` and inherited environment and npm config. It then hard-links the binary to `bin/mise`.
  - The script is pinned by the sha512 in `bun.lock`. The platform package is not in `bun.lock`, has no integrity hash, and is outside Bun's resolution and release-age controls.
  - The platform package version is fixed to the parent's version, and npm versions are immutable. So the realistic exposure is registry or mirror compromise, or a stolen token publishing a platform package that was never published for that version. The install runs with the user's npm credentials in the environment and then executes the binary on every hook.
  - Hidden requirement: `node` and `npm` must be on PATH at `bun install` time. If they are missing, the install fails. That is fail-closed, but it conflicts with the docs' "no global mise needed" for a Bun-only machine. `mise.toml` installs node only after mise exists.
  - Version range: `^2026.10.24` allows any 2026.x.y. `trustedDependencies` is keyed by name, so `bun update` would run a new, unreviewed preinstall under the existing trust. The repo already pins `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` exactly, and an exact pin `2026.10.24` is the better fit for a script-bearing dependency. Frozen-lockfile installs and CI are protected by the lockfile either way.
  - Recommend using the unscoped `mise` package instead, as the mise docs advise, pinned exactly, with `"mise"` in `trustedDependencies`. It matches the name `bunx mise` resolves to and has a single maintainer. That changes a dependency, so it is the root's decision.
- (Q3) Windows is unverified. The installer script for Windows rewrites `package.json` `bin` to `bin/mise.exe` after install and leaves a placeholder `bin/mise`. I could not determine whether Bun links its shim before or after the preinstall runs. The docs' claim that `bunx` "resolves the dev dependency … on POSIX and Windows alike" is therefore unsubstantiated. The installer also needs `npm.cmd`. I would soften that sentence or verify it on a Windows machine.
- Checked and found sound:
  - No attacker-controlled input reaches the shell in the installer: platform, arch and version are constants.
  - The `lefthook.yml` changes only prefix `bunx`; arguments are static.
  - `bunx lefthook install` in `scripts/prepare.ts` already used the same pattern.
  - The lockfile entry carries a sha512 and is consistent with `package.json`.
  - `mise.toml` hooks and tasks are repo-controlled, as before.

evidence:
- The bunx resolution and the trusted install script are each judged safe or not with evidence: bunx is acceptable with the `--no-install` hardening, and the trusted script is acceptable with an exact pin, but the explicit `trustedDependencies` list is a blocking regression.
  - bunx resolution: Bun source `src/cli/bunx_command.zig` (local `.bin` plus system PATH lookup, `--no-install` error path), `https://bun.sh/docs/cli/bunx`, Bun issues #5552 and #8154.
  - Registry facts for the `mise` and `@jdxcode/mise` packages: `https://registry.npmjs.org/mise/latest` and `https://registry.npmjs.org/@jdxcode%2fmise/latest`, same version, GitHub OIDC publisher.
  - mise docs, `https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html` ("Install `mise`, not the older `@jdxcode/mise`").
  - Installer script source: jdx/mise `scripts/release-npm.sh`.
  - `trustedDependencies` replacing the default list: `https://bun.com/docs/pm/lifecycle`, and Bun's `default-trusted-dependencies.txt` (lists both `lefthook` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`).
  - `hasInstallScript` in `/home/user/holyagent/bun.lock` lines 47 and 235.
  - CI dependency on the claude binary: `/home/user/holyagent-docs/.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 34 and 57-60.
  - Diff: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/1d4ee015-2de1-5dc0-aa17-15643c104828/scratchpad/mise-dep.diff`.
- findings: one blocking (the default trusted list is replaced, so `lefthook` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` scripts stop running), and three non-blocking (`bunx --no-install`, an exact pin or the unscoped `mise` package, and unverified Windows behavior), all described above. Not run: any `bun install`, `bunx`, or Windows check; the shipped 2026.10.24 installer file itself was not readable, so its content comes from the release script.
